title: Finite-length MRRW linear-programming bound
statement:
Fix natural numbers $n$, $t$, and $d$ with $t + 1 \le n$, and let $a$ be a real number lying strictly below every real zero of the Krawtchouk polynomial $K_t^{(n)}$. Suppose that the truncated Christoffel--Darboux kernel satisfies $\Phi_{n,t}(a, x) \le 0$ for every integer $x$ with $d \le x \le n$. Then the maximum size of a binary code of length $n$ and minimum distance $d$ is bounded by
\[
  A(n, d) \;\le\; \Phi_{n,t}(a, 0).
\]
hypotheses_covered: a is strictly less than every real zero of K_t^(n)
Φ_{n,t}(a,x) ≤ 0 for every integer x with d ≤ x ≤ n
